papers.title: Integrative multi-omic profiling reveals a spatially organized GPNMB⁺ monocyte-derived macrophage-NAMPT axis driving Th17 activation and fibrotic remodeling in cholestatic liver disease.
papers.authors: Chen J, Hu Y, Zhuang Q, Xu S, He C, Chen S, Yang C.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is characterized by chronic cholestasis, inflammatory bile duct injury, and progressive liver fibrosis. However, the spatial organization and key regulatory mechanisms of its inflammatory-fibrotic microenvironment remain poorly understood. We integrated large-scale single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets to construct a cellular and spatial atlas of PSC and incorporated multiple chronic fibrotic liver disease cohorts for cross-disease comparison. Key macrophage-T cell interactions and regulatory mechanisms were further evaluated using in vitro and in vivo experiments. PSC liver tissues showed reduced hepatocyte abundance, expansion of immune and stromal populations, and the formation of highly fibrotic niches within injury core and boundary regions. GPNMB+ monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) were detectable across multiple chronic liver diseases, but PSC-derived GPNMB+ MDMs exhibited stronger antigen-processing and MHC class II-mediated antigen-presentation programs. Spatial analyses further showed that GPNMB+ MDMs were associated with antigen-presentation, T-cell-associated, and extracellular matrix-remodeling programs in PSC lesions. Mechanistically, GPNMB+ MDMs promoted inflammatory activation and SLC7A5-associated metabolic remodeling in Th17-like T cells through NAMPT-mediated paracrine signaling. In vitro and in vivo experiments supported the contribution of NAMPT to cholestatic liver injury and fibrotic remodeling, while HMGA1 was identified as a potential upstream regulator of the GPNMB+ MDM state. This study identifies an HMGA1-NAMPT-Th17-like T cell-SLC7A5 axis in PSC, providing new insights into cholestatic liver fibrosis and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: γ-Terpinene modulates an HLA-centered antigen processing and presentation network at the tuberculosis-lung cancer molecular interface: an integrated computational and experimental study.
papers.authors: Saravanan S, Arockiasamy E, Chowmian H, Saravanan M.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) and lung cancer (LC) have common inflammatory and immune-regulatory pathways but there is still a lot of unknown about how they are related at a molecular level and whether they can be treated with some compounds. The present study employed an integrated computational and experimental strategy to investigate shared TB-LC molecular targets and to prioritize γ-terpinene as a candidate phytochemical targeting an HLA-centered antigen processing and presentation network. Targeted diseases were identified and then analyzed by protein-protein interaction network analysis, hub gene selection, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment. Molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations and MM/PBSA analysis were subsequently employed to characterize the predicted interactions of γ-terpinene with the prioritized HLA proteins. The computational analysis identified 103 shared TB-LC targets and highlighted HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DMA, HLA-DQA2 and HLA-DRA as central hub genes, with antigen processing and presentation among the prominent enriched biological pathways. Experimental validation in A549 and H-1299 lung cancer cells demonstrated concentration-dependent effects of γ-terpinene on cellular viability, accompanied by increased apoptotic populations and altered cell-cycle progression. Furthermore, γ-terpinene treatment modulated the expression of HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DMA, HLA-DQA2 and HLA-DRA at the transcript level, with protein-level validation performed for HLA-B, HLA-C and HLA-DRA. Collectively, these findings identify an HLA-centered antigen-processing and presentation network as a candidate molecular interface between tuberculosis and lung cancer and support further investigation of γ-terpinene-associated cellular responses. However, direct target engagement and a causal role for HLA modulation remain to be established in disease-relevant experimental models.

papers.title: Development of a Single B-Cell Platform for Producing Sheep Monoclonal Antibodies Against Bluetongue Virus.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Hu X, Li K, Song Y, Kassegn TA, Zhang G, Tian Z, Guan G, Niu Q, Shang Y, He J, Tang L, Du J.
papers.abstract: Bluetongue Virus (BTV) is a significant pathogen in ruminants, causing severe economic losses in livestock, particularly in sheep. Currently, the lack of technology for producing sheep-derived antibodies limits research on sheep immunology. Herein, we primarily established a sheep monoclonal antibody (mAb) production platform using single B cell antibody technology through fluorescence-activated cell sorting of specific B cells with IgM-CD21+BTV-1+ phenotype from sheep peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Using customized primers designed for nested single-cell PCR, we successfully amplified 43 variable-region sequences of paired heavy and light chains from 102 single sheep B cells. Ultimately, a panel of 39 sheep-derived mAbs with detectable strong binding to BTV-1 was identified, including clones with varying binding strengths by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, bio-layer interferometry, and immunofluorescence assay. Characterization of the 39 paired heavy and light chain sequences revealed biased germline gene usage of Oviari IGHV1S4-IGHJ6-01 and Oviari IGLV1-29-IGLJ2, and variations in the lengths of complementarity-determining region 3 among the recovered sequences. Notably, all recovered antibodies were lambda light chains. Collectively, we have developed a platform for producing sheep single B-cell mAbs using BTV as a model antigen. This platform provides an approach for dissecting sheep humoral immune responses and lays the groundwork for developing therapeutic and diagnostic antibodies against other sheep pathogens.

papers.title: Kawasaki disease: integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation reveal novel biomarkers KLHL42 and SOS2.
papers.authors: Ma J, Zhang T, He W, Gao N, Mu Z, Wan X, Ma L, Yan X.
papers.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute self-limited vasculitis whose relationship with the gut microbial metabolite butyrate remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the association between Kawasaki disease (KD) and butyrate-related genes. Public databases were utilized to obtain KD-related transcriptomic datasets and butyrate-related genes. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were applied, identifying 51 candidate genes. Mendelian randomization analysis was conducted to evaluate causal relationships between genes and KD. Expression levels of key genes were validated using public datasets and clinical samples. A nomogram based on identified biomarkers was constructed and its predictive performance was assessed. Functional enrichment analysis was applied to explore biological pathways involved. Immune cell infiltration analysis and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) were used to characterize expression patterns of target genes across cell types and during differentiation. Differential expression analysis and WGCNA identified 51 candidate genes. Mendelian randomization revealed that SOS2and GAS6were risk factors for KD, while KLHL42was a protective factor. Validation in public datasets and clinical samples showed that compared to controls, KLHL42expression was downregulated and SOS2expression was upregulated in KD patients. The nomogram constructed based on KLHL42and SOS2demonstrated good predictive performance. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that both KLHL42and SOS2were significantly associated with the chemokine signaling pathway and correlated closely with infiltration abundances of neutrophils and CD8⁺ T cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis suggested that T cells, B cells, and monocytes were potentially key cell types in KD; expression levels of KLHL42and SOS2gradually decreased during T-cell differentiation but increased during B-cell and monocyte differentiation. This study identifies genes associated with butyrate-related host responses in Kawasaki disease, providing clues for further mechanistic investigation. This study employed transcriptomic analysis and Mendelian randomization to reveal the association characteristics between Kawasaki disease and genes related to butyrate. It identified KLHL42 and SOS2 as biomarkers, with SOS2 determined to be a risk factor and KLHL42 a protective factor, validated in clinical samples. This research provides novel therapeutic targets for investigating the pathological mechanisms of Kawasaki disease.

papers.title: The deep learning framework Hist2Prot infers single-cell spatial proteomics from histology to predict biomarkers and clinical outcomes.
papers.authors: Fan J, Yang S, Hu E, An J, Liu Q, Liu N, Ma M, Prystowsky M, Lv T, Yeo SY, Ren Y, Liu Y, Li L, Li Y, Sun Q, Qian P, Lu L, Deng W, Pan X, Yin S.
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics enables high-resolution mapping of protein expression within the tumor microenvironment, but its routine clinical application remains limited by cost, technical complexity and restricted tissue coverage. Here we present Hist2Prot, a deep learning framework that generates single-cell spatial proteomic profiles from routine hematoxylin and eosin histology. Trained on approximately 51 million paired cells from a same-section G4X spatial proteomics dataset, Hist2Prot was evaluated in internal test cohorts, independent same-platform G4X cohorts and external cross-platform datasets comprising approximately 72 million additional cells, showing concordance with measured protein profiles and outperforming established baselines. Hist2Prot-derived virtual proteins preserved immune, stromal and tumor cell phenotypes and recapitulated clinically relevant tumor microenvironment organization. Across seven independent patient cohorts comprising 1,774 patients, virtual spatial proteomics improved molecular biomarker, prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction beyond hematoxylin and eosin morphology alone. Hist2Prot enables scalable single-cell computational spatial proteomics from routine histology for precision oncology.

papers.title: Generative AI-Designed Immunoglobulin Domain Antibodies (IgDAbs) Against the Fusion Protein as a Neutralizing Agent for Respiratory Syncytial Virus.
papers.authors: Prasad YR, Khandave PY, Ratnaparkhe M, Kendre AG, Bharatam PV, Pande AH.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to rationally design, screen, and experimentally validate novel immunoglobulin domain antibodies (IgDAbs) targeting the site II epitope of the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion (F) protein using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) driven tools. A generative AI tool was employed to generate 250 novel IgDAb sequences optimized for RSV-F site II binding. Candidates were screened computationally using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to select hit candidates. The selected IgDAbs were cloned and produced using an E. coli expression system. Purified IgDAbs were characterized for target specificity via ELISA and evaluated for functional viral inhibition using in vitro microneutralization assay against RSV A2 (long strain). Computational screening narrowed the library to 05 structurally compatible hit IgDAb with predicted binding affinity. ELISA confirmed specific binding of purified IgDAbs to the RSV-F protein. In vitro microneutralization assays demonstrated neutralization of RSV A2 (long strain), with two 'lead' IgDAbs showing EC50 of 1.3 µg/mL and 3.5 µg/mL. Combining generative AI sequence generation with an integrated in silico and in vitro screening cascade enables the rapid, cost-effective discovery of neutralizing nanobodies against RSV, offering a viable alternative to resource-intensive traditional antibody discovery workflows.

papers.title: CAPG beyond actin capping: Molecular regulation, cancer progression, and therapeutic resistance.
papers.authors: Yang JW, Wang L, Zhao L, Jiao PP, Chen SY, Yang L.
papers.abstract: Macrophage-capping protein (CAPG) is a calcium- and phosphoinositide-regulated member of the gelsolin superfamily that reversibly caps the barbed ends of actin filaments without intrinsic severing activity. Although initially characterized as a cytoskeletal regulator, CAPG displays dynamic cytoplasmic, nuclear, and nucleolar localization and is increasingly recognized as a multifunctional protein involved in cellular signaling, transcriptional regulation, and stress adaptation. Beyond its physiological roles in macrophage function, membrane remodeling, intracellular trafficking, and mechanoadaptation, dysregulated CAPG has been implicated in a range of pathological conditions, most prominently cancer. In many malignancies, elevated CAPG expression is associated with tumor growth, migration, invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, metastasis, and unfavorable clinical outcomes, although context-dependent tumor-suppressive observations have also been reported. Mechanistically, CAPG contributes to malignant progression through both actin-dependent processes and non-canonical signaling and transcriptional programs, including NF-κB-, PI3K-AKT-, ERK-, Wnt/β-catenin-, and Hippo/YAP-associated pathways. Increasing evidence further links CAPG to resistance to cisplatin, paclitaxel, gemcitabine, doxorubicin, and sorafenib through mechanisms involving transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, pro-survival signaling, and antioxidant adaptation. Emerging preclinical studies additionally suggest that CAPG may influence ferroptosis-associated responses in selected tumor contexts, although the generality and clinical relevance of this relationship remain to be established. Single-cell and spatial studies have also revealed CAPG expression in both malignant cells and macrophage populations, highlighting its potential relevance to therapy-adapted cellular states and the tumor microenvironment. Emerging nanobody-based and small-molecule studies indicate that CAPG is functionally targetable, although selective pharmacological inhibitors remain unavailable. This review summarizes the molecular regulation, physiological functions, pathological roles, cancer-associated mechanisms, and therapeutic potential of CAPG, with particular emphasis on treatment resistance, tumor-immune interactions, signaling-dependent adaptation, and emerging redox- and ferroptosis-associated mechanisms.

papers.title: Depletion of Endogenous IL-18 Suppresses Pancreatic Cancer Progression, Reprograms the Tumor Microenvironment, and Enhances KRAS Inhibitor Efficacy.
papers.authors: Sun X, Ma Y, Wang L, Gao J, Fei Y, Zhang X, Tino RB, Kim Y, Wang H, Lin K, Zhang D, Zhao Z, Lin C, Shen JP, Lin SH, Wang L, Bernard V, Koay EJ, Zhao D, Wang H, Jiang W, Kim BYS, Maitra A, Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits a highly complex tumor microenvironment enriched with both inflammatory and immunosuppressive factors. Interleukin-18 (IL-18), a cytokine of the IL-1 family, is elevated in PDAC and correlates with poor patient outcomes. However, the functional role of IL-18 in PDAC progression and immune regulation remains poorly defined. We generated genetically engineered mouse models with IL-18 depletion in the context of spontaneous PDAC development. Single-cell RNA-sequencing and functional assays were used to analyze PDAC progression, macrophage phenotypes, and cancer cell-macrophage interactions. Mechanistic studies were performed to determine the effects of IL-18 on STAT1 signaling and CD47 expression. The role of IL-18 in therapeutic response was evaluated using KRAS inhibitor (KRASi) treatment models. Elevated IL-18 expression correlated with poor patient survival. Genetic depletion of IL-18 significantly suppressed spontaneous PDAC progression and prolonged survival in mice. Mechanistically, IL-18 promoted cancer cell survival by activating STAT1-dependent CD47 expression, thereby impairing macrophage-mediated phagocytosis of cancer cells. In addition, IL-18 depletion reshaped the tumor immune microenvironment by enriching macrophage populations with enhanced antigen-presenting and phagocytic phenotypes characterized by increased MHCII and CD11c expression. Notably, KRAS inhibitor treatment further increased IL-18 expression in PDAC cells, whereas IL-18 depletion enhanced macrophage-mediated clearance of KRASi-treated cancer cells and improved therapeutic efficacy. IL-18 promotes pancreatic cancer progression by enabling cancer cell survival and immune evasion through macrophage reprogramming. Targeting IL-18 may represent a therapeutic strategy to enhance macrophage-mediated anti-tumor immunity and improve responses to KRAS inhibitor therapies in PDAC.

papers.title: Decoding cancer therapy resistance through advanced 3D organoid systems.
papers.authors: Ye R, Wang J, Xu W, Chen Y, Zhang Z, Zhang Y, Qin S.
papers.abstract: Precision oncology still faces low clinical translation rates. This is largely because two-dimensional (2D) culture systems cannot reproduce tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental stress. Here, we review the applications of 3D cancer models, including scaffold-free spheroids, patient-derived organoids (PDOs) biobanks, and microphysiological systems (MPSs), in drug resistance modeling and personalized therapy. These platforms effectively model metabolic gradients, lineage plasticity, and immunological features within the tumor microenvironment (TME), thereby bridging the genotype-phenotype gap. They also capture physical immune exclusion, T cell exhaustion, and antigen presentation to facilitate the evaluation of immunotherapies. Last, we discuss key translational bottlenecks such as standardization and throughput, proposing the integration of advanced biomanufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven phenomics, and computational modeling to develop 3D cancer platforms into clinical predictive systems for optimizing precision treatment strategies.

papers.title: PARP inhibitors in breast cancer: From DNA repair targeting to next-generation precision therapeutics.
papers.authors: Yaringaño J, Pimentel I, Thomas-Bonafos T, Oliveira M, Saura C, Ouali K, Grinda T, Rassy E, Pistilli B, Balmaña J, Ribeiro JM.
papers.abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) have established synthetic lethality as a clinically validated therapeutic strategy in breast cancer. Olaparib and talazoparib improve outcomes in HER2-negative metastatic disease among patients with germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants, while adjuvant olaparib reduces recurrence and mortality in high-risk, HER2-negative early breast cancer. However, their clinical utility remains constrained by acquired resistance, hematologic toxicity, and limitations in biomarker-based patient selection. This review examines the pharmacological determinants of PARPi activity, including catalytic inhibition and PARP trapping, and summarizes clinical evidence across disease stages and molecular subgroups, including germline PALB2 and somatic BRCA1/2 alterations. We discuss primary and acquired resistance mechanisms, particularly homologous recombination restoration through BRCA1/2 reversion mutations, and the potential of circulating tumor DNA to monitor clonal evolution. We also assess biomarkers spanning genomic scars, functional homologous recombination status, and PARP target engagement, with emphasis on RAD51 foci assays and emerging computational and imaging approaches. Finally, we review next-generation PARP1-selective inhibitors and rational combinations with immunotherapy, topoisomerase I inhibitor-based antibody-drug conjugates, chemotherapy, and other DNA damage response agents. These strategies may widen the therapeutic window, refine patient selection, and inform treatment sequencing, but prospective validation is required before their routine clinical integration.

papers.title: Characterization of TLR4 and BCL2 as potential PANoptosis biomarkers in spinal cord injury.
papers.authors: Bai Y, Yu M, Zhang T, Dong W, Huang Y, Yuan J, Wang R, Chu X, Li Q, Wang R.
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes extensive programmed cell death in neural cells, involving apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis, a process collectively termed PANoptosis. However, direct markers of PANoptosome activation in SCI remain lacking. This study integrated bioinformatics and machine learning with in vitro and in vivo experiments to screen and expression-validate candidate PANoptosis-related genes for SCI. Three SCI transcriptomic datasets (human, rat, and mouse) were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). We screened differentially expressed PANoptosis-related genes (DE-PRGs), and applied functional enrichment, PPI analysis and two machine-learning algorithms to screen hub genes. Hub genes were cross-dataset-validated for expression and exploratory discriminative performance, and their correlations with estimated peripheral blood immune cell proportions were analyzed. TLR4 and BCL2 were further validated in a rat spinal cord hemisection model and an LPS-induced BV2 microglial inflammation model using immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, and Western blot. Intersection of PPI topology and machine-learning outputs yielded six candidate hub genes: IL1B, TLR3, TLR4, CASP1, IFNG, and BCL2. Cross-validation across human, rat, and mouse datasets revealed consistent statistically-significant expression changes for TLR4. BCL2 showed significant alterations in human and rat datasets, but not in mouse data. ROC analysis based solely on public transcriptomic datasets showed discriminative ability for TLR4 (AUC = 0.805) and BCL2 (AUC = 1.000, in the human dataset; the BCL2 estimate should be interpreted cautiously because of cross-species inconsistency and limited sample size). CIBERSORT analysis indicated that both genes were correlated with estimated proportions of circulating immune cell subsets. Both in vivo and in vitro experiments showed consistent TLR4 upregulation and BCL2 downregulation (p < 0.05), consistent with bioinformatics predictions. TLR4 and BCL2 are candidate PANoptosis-related genes in SCI, with cross-species and experimental expression evidence. These findings provide a basis for further functional studies to determine their roles in PANoptosis and secondary injury, rather than establishing them as prospective clinical biomarkers.

papers.title: Classic Hodgkin Lymphoma: Biology-Driven Disease Model.
papers.authors: Carbone A, Gloghini A.
papers.abstract: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is a unique lymphoid neoplasm in which rare malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg (HRS) cells orchestrate an extensive, spatially organized immune and inflammatory microenvironment that determines diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic sensitivity. This review summarizes recent advances in the biopathology, diagnosis, and prognostic stratification of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, with particular emphasis on the emerging molecular subtyping framework proposed by Aoki and colleagues, which is not yet clinically validated, and on the proposed concept of classic Hodgkin lymphoma as a systemic immunobiological disease. In this narrative review, we examined the literature on classic Hodgkin lymphoma biology, the tumor immune microenvironment, diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers, and molecular classification, prioritizing studies published through to mid-2026 and distinguishing established evidence from observational associations, preclinical findings, meeting abstracts, ongoing trials, and hypotheses, including single-cell, spatial, and liquid biopsy technologies, and integrating the authors' own recent work on immune and inflammatory biomarkers and on the systemic immunobiological features of classic Hodgkin lymphoma. Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells sustain disease through constitutive NF-κB and JAK/STAT signaling, 9p24.1-driven PD-L1/PD-L2 overexpression, and secretion of chemokines and cytokines that recruit and functionally reprogram CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, macrophages, and stromal cells. Multidimensional profiling integrating malignant-cell genomics, spatial transcriptomics, and imaging mass cytometry has led to the proposal of four molecular subtypes of classic Hodgkin lymphoma (CST, CN913, STB, and CN2P), each defined by distinct genomic drivers and immune architecture, a hypothesis-generating framework that awaits prospective validation. Classic Hodgkin lymphoma has been proposed to be a systemic immunobiological disorder, with circulating tumor DNA, thymus and activation-regulated chemokine (TARC/CCL17), and peripheral immune signatures associated with disease activity beyond the lymph node; these markers are promising but remain investigational. Diagnosis is evolving from morphology-based assessment toward precision immunopathology integrating spatial and digital pathology, while prognosis is progressively incorporating tissue-based, circulating, spatial, and molecular biomarkers into integrated risk models that are, for the most part, still investigational and are being tested in biomarker-directed clinical trials. The convergence of molecular subtyping, spatial immunobiology, systemic disease biology, and liquid biopsy may reshape the diagnostic and prognostic landscape of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, suggesting a potential transition from anatomically defined, morphology-based assessment toward integrated, biology-driven precision medicine. This transition has unfolded stepwise, from tissue-based immunophenotyping and spatial biomarkers, through circulating markers such as ctDNA and TARC/CCL17, to genomically defined molecular subtypes now being linked to systemic immune readouts and tested in biomarker-directed trials. Prospective validation, assay standardization, and evidence of clinical utility are required before these approaches can enter routine practice.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Ribosome Biogenesis-Associated Molecular Subtypes and Immune Characteristics in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Zhang S, Gao H, Ma Y, Gao S, Yang J, Li L.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity. We integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to investigate associations between ribosome biogenesis-related (RiboSis-related) gene expression and the molecular and immune characteristics of HCC. GLUL+ hepatocytes had the highest RiboSis-related gene-set score among hepatocyte subpopulations, and ligand-receptor analysis inferred an MDK-SDC2 interaction between ALDOA+ and GLUL+ hepatocytes. Feature selection identified four candidate genes, with subsequent subtype analysis highlighting BOP1 and EXOSC4. The two molecular subtypes differed in RiboSis-related gene expression, immune cell signature scores, mutation profiles, checkpoint gene expression, and TIDE scores. Immunohistochemistry showed higher BOP1 and EXOSC4 staining in HCC than in paired adjacent tissues. EXOSC4 staining was lower in HBV-associated than in non-viral HCC within the tissue microarray. These findings associate RiboSis-related expression with distinct molecular and inferred immune features in HCC. The clinical relevance of these subtypes for immunotherapy and the functional roles of BOP1 and EXOSC4 require further validation.

papers.title: LLPS-Driven Membraneless Organelle Activity Landscape Reveals Molecular Subtypes, Immune States, and Prognostic Stratification in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Yan H, Yang N, Zhang L, Tian H, Mo W, Lan M, Lin Z, Lin H, Wang Z, Zou J, He F, Sun J.
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of membraneless organelles (MLOs) that regulate cellular compartmentalization and diverse biological processes. However, the landscape and clinical relevance of MLO-associated activity in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain unclear. We integrated curated MLO-associated gene sets with transcriptomic data to estimate MLO activity using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. MLO-related molecular subtypes were identified via consensus clustering, and an integrative machine learning framework was used to develop and validate the Membraneless Organelle Risk Score (MLORS) across independent cohorts. We further examined associations of MLORS with immune features, genomic alterations, and predicted treatment sensitivity and evaluated the function and phase-separation properties of E2F7 in vitro. MLO-associated activity was broadly dysregulated in LUAD, with high-MLO and low-MLO subtypes exhibiting distinct immune profiles and survival outcomes. High MLORS was associated with poorer survival, a computationally inferred immune-suppressed microenvironmental profile, higher tumor mutational burden, and lower predicted sensitivity to selected EGFR-targeted agents and chemotherapy. E2F7 formed nuclear condensates with LLPS-like properties and promoted lung cancer cell proliferation and migration in vitro. These findings link transcriptionally inferred MLO activity to the heterogeneity and prognosis of LUAD, support MLORS as a candidate prognostic stratification tool, and identify E2F7 phase-separation behavior as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

papers.title: Metabolomics in Thoracic Oncology from Biomarker Discovery to Therapeutic Targeting: A Narrative Review.
papers.authors: Mahmoud MA, Sharma G, Sarkaria IS, Porembka MR, DeBerardinis RJ, Kernstine KH.
papers.abstract: Thoracic malignancies show context-dependent metabolic plasticity that influences growth, immune evasion, and treatment response. This review examines how metabolomics, stable-isotope tracing, and metabolic flux analysis complement molecular profiling in lung, esophageal, pleural, and thymic cancers. We distinguish metabolite abundance from isotope enrichment and quantitative flux, and review analytical platforms, computational workflows, histology-specific programs, immunometabolism, biomarkers, and therapy. Lung squamous cell carcinoma often depends on glycolysis, lung adenocarcinoma shows substrate and spatial heterogeneity, and molecular subsets of small cell lung cancer have preclinical vulnerabilities in arginine metabolism and guanosine nucleotide synthesis. Hypoxia and metabolite exchange among malignant, stromal, and immune cells may shape therapeutic resistance. Biofluid and tissue studies support early detection and monitoring, but most circulating signatures and findings in rare thoracic tumors remain exploratory. Translation is limited by confounding, incomplete metabolite identification, small cohorts, and limited external validation. Trials of unselected metabolic inhibitors have largely failed. Two biomarker-selected strategies have advanced: arginine deprivation in non-epithelioid pleural mesothelioma, a population enriched for argininosuccinate synthetase 1 (ASS1) deficiency, and PRMT5 inhibition in tumors with MTAP deletion. These results suggest that success may depend on selecting patients by a demonstrated metabolic dependency rather than by the plausibility of the target. Progress requires harmonized multicenter workflows, paired tissue and biofluid sampling, rigorous validation, and integration with spatial, single-cell, multi-omic, and clinical data.

papers.title: When SERS silent-region nanoprobes meet bacteriophage-based nanoarchitectonics: A highly sensitive and reliable biosensing platform for detection of Salmonella typhimurium.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Huang J, Zhang X, Qiu M, Yang Y, Li Z, Jiang Y, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) demonstrates great potential for pathogen detection due to its fingerprint recognition capability and rapid response. However, existing SERS methods still face challenges in the aspects of sensitivity and specificity, especially in complex samples. Herein, a Raman silent-region sandwich-type SERS biosensing platform was constructed for ultrasensitive and specific detection of Salmonella typhimurium (S. typhimurium) using antibody(Ab) -conjugated gold nanobipyramids (AuNBPs)@Prussian blue (PB) (AuNBP@PB) SERS probes. In this platform, the plasmonic probes were engineered by combining AuNBP@PB core-shell nanoparticles with antibodies, enabling stable silent-region SERS signal generation and specific bacterial labeling. Meanwhile, phages were pre-oriented on magnetic beads through electrostatic adsorption and then covalently stabilized, forming a stable capture unit that improved the capture efficiency of S. typhimurium. Importantly, the effects of AuNBP aspect ratio (AR) and PB shell thickness on SERS signals were investigated, and the strongest silent-region Raman signal was obtained at an AuNBP AR of 3.25 and a PB shell thickness of 15 nm. Benefiting from phage-mediated magnetic enrichment and AuNBP@PB-Ab-mediated silent-region SERS immunoprobes, the Raman silent-region sandwich-type SERS platform has achieved sensitive and specific detection of S. typhimurium with a limit of detection of 1 CFU/mL. In addition, machine learning-assisted analysis was further introduced to improve identification and quantification reliability. The random forest classifier distinguished positive and negative samples and located the key variables mainly in the PB C ≡ N vibration region at 2147-2157 cm-1, while Gaussian process regression refined concentration prediction under matrix interference. Overall, this work provides a Raman silent-region SERS biosensing strategy for sensitive pathogen detection.

papers.title: Single cell transcriptome analysis reveals disease severity-associated B cell subpopulations in COVID-19 patients.
papers.authors: Ren Y, Jiang X, Yan M, Liu L, Fan J, Niu X, Ji G, Cao H, Shao F.
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms of B cell activation is critical for elucidating immune dysregulation in Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). B cells play a central role in humoral immunity by differentiating into plasma cells that produce antibodies against SARS-CoV-2. However, the cellular pathways controlling this process remain unclear in severe disease. Here, we analyzed single-cell transcriptome datasets (GSE155224) from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of COVID-19 patients, and found that B cell frequencies were significantly elevated in patients with progressive disease compared to stable cases. Notably, we identified a distinct B cell subpopulation, termed CD70+ naive B cells, characterized by high CD70 gene expression. The adaptive immune activation and anti-viral response of this CD70+ naive B cell subset were markedly diminished. Flow cytometry and gene expression analyses revealed a transcriptional signature consistent with STAT3/PAX5-BCL6 activation in CD70+ naive B cells. This signature was associated with a lower plasma-cell fraction, and genes related to adaptive immune activation and antiviral responses were expressed at lower levels in these cells. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing with flow cytometry, we revealed that the accumulation of CD70+ naive B cells is associated with disease severity in COVID-19. Our findings suggest that aberrant expression of CD70 and activation of the STAT3/PAX5-BCL6 axis in naive B cells may be associated with lower expression of antibody-related genes and with poor clinical outcomes. Targeting this pathway could provide new therapeutic opportunities or biomarkers for managing severe COVID-19.

papers.title: Senescence-Related Transcriptomic Analysis and Functional Characterization of ANGPTL4 in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Shi Y, Zhang H, Jiang Y, Li X, Sun D.
papers.abstract: Background: Cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) can alter communication between tumor cells and the surrounding microenvironment, but the extracellular mediators involved in this process remain poorly defined in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods: Bulk transcriptomic analysis was used to characterize senescence-related transcriptional alterations and construct a prognostic signature. ANGPTL4 expression was evaluated in public datasets and clinical samples. Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis was then performed to map senescence-associated gene-set scores across LUAD cell populations and to examine the cell-cell communication. ANGPTL4 depletion and overexpression were used to assess its effects on LUAD-cell proliferation, migration, and SA-β-gal positivity, while a subcutaneous xenograft model was used to examine tumor growth in vivo. Conditioned-medium and indirect co-culture experiments were performed to assess the effects of ANGPTL4-overexpressing LUAD cells on THP-1-derived macrophage inflammatory responses, and MCC950 was used to evaluate the contribution of NLRP3-associated signaling. Results: Senescence-related transcriptional alterations in LUAD were enriched in inflammatory and immune-related pathways. ANGPTL4 was included in a five-gene prognostic model and selected for functional investigation because it encodes a secreted protein. We found that ANGPTL4 protein levels were increased in LUAD tissues. Single-cell analysis showed relatively high senescence-associated gene-set scores in macrophage-enriched populations, together with stronger cell-cell communication in the higher-score group. ANGPTL4 depletion reduced LUAD-cell migration and SA-β-gal positivity, while its overexpression had the opposite effects and resulted in larger xenograft tumors. Conditioned medium and indirect co-culture experiments showed that ANGPTL4-overexpressing LUAD cells induced inflammatory changes in THP-1-derived macrophages, accompanied by increased NLRP3-associated markers and IL-1β secretion. These changes were partly attenuated by MCC950. Conclusions: These findings suggest that ANGPTL4 is associated with tumor cell-macrophage crosstalk in LUAD and may correlate with senescence-related transcriptional signatures, while the specific biological role of ANGPTL4 remains to be further characterized.

papers.title: Identification of a DNA Damage Response-Related Prognostic Signature and Functional Validation of SMC3 in Glioma.
papers.authors: Ma J, Zhang C, Zhang J, Zhong C.
papers.abstract: DNA damage response (DDR) deficiencies are linked to tumorigenesis and progression. However, the association of DDR with prognosis and therapeutic response in glioma has not been fully illustrated. TCGA and CGGA databases were used to acquire RNA-seq and clinical data about gliomas. LASSO-Cox regression was introduced to establish a DDR-based risk signature. The single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) algorithm was used to estimate immune infiltrates. The performance of the signature and nomogram in predicting survival was evaluated using ROC curves. Connectivity Map (CMap) analysis was used to nominate candidate compounds, and pRRophetic was used to predict drug sensitivity. Through LASSO-Cox regression, we developed a prognostic risk score based on five DDR-related genes (GADD45G, HDAC1, RRM2, SMC3, and WEE1). Higher risk scores were associated with shorter overall survival and remained significant in multivariable Cox analyses. A prognostic nomogram achieved 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs of 0.901, 0.936, and 0.903 in TCGA and 0.776, 0.816, and 0.802 in CGGA, respectively. High-risk tumors showed enrichment of TNFα signaling via NFκB and IL6/JAK/STAT3 gene sets, together with differences in inferred immune cell-associated features and immune checkpoint gene expression. Computational drug sensitivity analyses associated higher risk scores with lower predicted IC50 values for GSK269962A, pazopanib, rapamycin, and NVP-BEZ235, providing hypotheses for subsequent experimental validation. SMC3 overexpression inhibited glioma cell proliferation and migration in vitro. The DDR-related signature showed prognostic value and associations with immune-related transcriptional features in glioma, with in vitro evidence suggesting a functional role for SMC3.

papers.title: Hypoxia-Associated Glycolytic-Lipogenic Reprogramming and Impaired Antigen Presentation in SPP1 + Tumor-Associated Macrophages in Ovarian Cancer.
papers.authors: Zuo X, Huang S, Li Y, Wang Z, Xue H, Min J, Hong L, Li S.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer has an immunosuppressive microenvironment in which SPP1+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are linked to poor prognosis and immune evasion, yet their molecular features and metabolic mechanisms remain unclear. We therefore set out to determine whether SPP1 marks a discrete TAM subpopulation or a functional state in treatment-naïve high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), to define the transcriptional and metabolic program that accompanies it, and to test whether local hypoxia is associated with it. Tumor-derived, treatment-naïve samples from three single-cell datasets (one lesion per patient; 47 patients) yielded 385,504 cells; Seurat v5 and Harmony were used for clustering, annotation, and batch correction. SPP1+/SPP1- macrophages were compared by differential expression, GO/KEGG/GSEA, metabolic scoring, and transcription factor inference, and the definition was retested with within-sample SPP1-high versus SPP1-low comparisons and with MSigDB Hallmark gene sets scored by two independent algorithms. Validation used Visium spatial transcriptomics (GSE263920), TCGA-OV (n = 429), CD8+ T cell exhaustion analysis, CellChat and a syngeneic ID8 model. Of 64,067 macrophages (16.62%), 82.0% were SPP1+; upregulated genes were enriched in glycolysis, monocyte migration and tissue remodeling, whereas MHC class II and neutrophil-related genes were downregulated. At the sample level, glycolysis, fatty acid synthesis and glutaminolysis scores were elevated and the cholesterol synthesis score was reduced, with no evidence of suppressed fatty acid oxidation or oxidative phosphorylation; HIF1A ranked 4th and NR1H3 3rd among 271 transcription factors. All 8 spatial sections showed positive hypoxia-SPP1 correlations, and hotspots showed elevated glycolysis, EMT, immunosuppression and macrophage scores. No robust association was found between SPP1+ TAM infiltration and CD8+ T cell exhaustion (p = 0.315). MDK-LRP1/SDC1 was the major macrophage-directed input. Immunofluorescence showed SPP1 immunoreactivity in a subset of CD68+ macrophages within HIF1α-rich areas of ID8 tumors, without CD8+PD-1+ T cell aggregation. SPP1+ TAMs therefore correspond to a hypoxic functional state with HIF1A activation, a glycolytic-lipogenic transcriptional program, reduced cholesterol synthesis gene expression and a reduced MHC class II program; protein-level and functional validation, and direct tests of HIF1A dependency, remain necessary.

papers.title: Stachydrine Hydrochloride Suppresses Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Reprogramming Macrophage Polarization Through the LIF/PI3K/Akt Axis.
papers.authors: Bao X, Zhang Y, Sun L, He C, Li D, Shi X, Ma Y.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) carries a poor prognosis, largely owing to an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) shaped by M2-polarized tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). Stachydrine hydrochloride (SH), an alkaloid derived from Panzeria alashanica Kupr., exerts anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor effects; however, its immunomodulatory action in HCC remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether SH restrains HCC progression by regulating TAM polarization through the LIF/PI3K/AKT pathway, using RAW264.7, THP-1, HepG2, and Huh-7 cells; a subcutaneous tumor model; and bioinformatic analysis of clinical samples. SH modulated macrophage phenotypes dose-dependently without obvious cytotoxicity, promoting M1 polarization while suppressing M2 polarization and autophagy in M2 macrophages, and enhanced macrophage phagocytosis of HCC cells. Conditioned medium from SH-treated M2 macrophages inhibited HCC cell proliferation, migration, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Mechanistically, SH suppressed LIF/PI3K/AKT activation in M2 macrophages, and LIF overexpression showed a trending capacity to partially counteract SH-mediated M2-suppressive effects. Bioinformatics linked high M2-TAM infiltration with poor HCC prognosis. In vivo, SH retarded tumor growth, decreased intratumoral M2-TAM infiltration, and reduced Ki-67 levels. Collectively, SH remodels the TIME to restrain HCC progression, and these effects are associated with inhibition of M2-TAM polarization and attenuation of LIF/PI3K/Akt signaling, revealing a novel immunotherapeutic mechanism and supporting SH as a promising natural agent for HCC immunotherapy.

papers.title: Biomarkers for Cancer Immunotherapy: Advances, Challenges, and Clinical Applications.
papers.authors: Ahmed A, Haq F.
papers.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has revolutionized oncology by harnessing the immune system to recognize and eliminate malignant cells. Despite remarkable clinical successes, a substantial proportion of patients fail to respond or develop resistance, highlighting the urgent need for reliable biomarkers to guide patient selection, predict therapeutic outcomes, and monitor treatment responses. This review addresses both the emerging and established biomarkers for cancer immunotherapy. These include molecular, cellular, and systemic biomarkers within tumor tissues, blood, and the tumor microenvironment. The principal ones include immune checkpoint-related biomarkers (e.g., programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression), tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability, neoantigen profiling, circulating tumor DNA, and immune cell signatures. We grade each biomarker by analytical validity, clinical validity, clinical utility and regulatory readiness; place it in one of four evidence tiers; and outline the steps needed to bring candidate markers into the clinic. Recent developments in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence, and single-cell analysis are accelerating biomarker discovery, providing a clearer understanding of tumor-immune interactions. Furthermore, the integration of dynamic biomarkers is critical for optimally refining therapeutic strategies for real-time monitoring and detection of resistance mechanisms. This review aims to provide a worldwide overview of present achievements, challenges, and future opportunities in biomarker research and ultimately enable the development of more personalized and effective strategies for immunotherapy of cancer.

papers.title: Transcriptome Analysis Reveals the Role of Partial Lymphatic Vessel Ligation in Rats with Cirrhotic Portal Hypertension.
papers.authors: Wu Z, Luo G, Zhao J, Zhou Q, Li H, Zhang C, Wu G, Fan Q, Qi X, Huo H, Lin J, Luo M, Zheng L.
papers.abstract: The liver lymphatic system plays an essential role during the progression of cirrhotic portal hypertension (PHT), featuring significantly enhanced lymphangiogenesis. However, the role of liver lymphatic functional drainage is understudied in cirrhosis. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the effects of partial lymphatic vessel ligation (PLVL) of the liver on PHT. The rat model was established by common bile duct ligation (BDL), when PLVL was achieved via ligation of the portal and celiac lymph node. The severity of cirrhosis and PHT were evaluated, as well as macrophage infiltration and lymphangiogenesis. Bulk RNA-seq of liver was used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Datasets of single-cell and bulk RNA-seq were obtained from the GEO database. Human dermal lymphatic endothelial cells (hLECs) were used for in vitro validation. Ligation of lymphatic drainage caused significant deterioration of liver cirrhosis and PHT in BDL rats. Our bulk RNA-seq suggested significant enrichment of vascular remodeling and angiogenesis-related pathways, as well as lipid metabolism-related biological functions in BDL rats after PLVL. Further analysis combined with public datasets identified several endothelial cell-specific upregulated genes in BDL and PLVL rats. LEC-derived upregulated genes were also identified from bulk RNA-seq of LECs isolated from mice liver, which were validated by incubating hLECs in TNF-α, LPS, TGF-β1. In the current study, we provide the first evidence that liver lymphatic drainage blockade aggravates BDL-induced cirrhotic PHT. LEC-associated secretory proteins might play a potential role in PHT progression, when hepatic inflammation and immune response are considered to be the essential regulatory mechanisms.

papers.title: TSPO and LRBA Expression Is Associated with Acute Renal Allograft Rejection: An Integrative Transcriptomic Analysis.
papers.authors: Yi S, Zhu Q, Chen S.
papers.abstract: Acute renal transplant rejection causes allograft injury and affects long-term graft survival. Mitophagy helps maintain mitochondrial homeostasis and regulate immune function, but its relationship with acute rejection remains unclear. We integrated public renal allograft transcriptomic datasets using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and machine learning. We performed external cohort validation, survival analysis, immune deconvolution, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, virtual knockout analysis, and quantitative PCR in mouse renal allografts. Among 32 shared mitophagy-associated genes which we identified, TSPO was consistently upregulated and LRBA was downregulated across independent biopsy cohorts. An exploratory TSPO/LRBA two-gene model showed modest discrimination between rejection and non-rejection samples. Higher model scores were associated with poorer graft survival. An exploratory analysis of the model was then performed in peripheral blood. Functional and single-cell analyses linked these genes to monocyte/macrophage populations, antigen presentation, T-cell signaling, and inflammatory pathways. Virtual knockout analysis predicted changes in antigen presentation, phagocytosis, and allograft rejection pathways. Quantitative PCR confirmed increased TSPO and decreased LRBA expression in mouse renal allografts with acute rejection. Together, these findings identify TSPO and LRBA as new candidate mitophagy-associated biomarkers linked to monocytes/macrophages and support further investigation of their associations with acute renal transplant rejection.

papers.title: Characterization of Clonixeril as a Positive Modulator of DMXAA-Induced Murine STING Signaling.
papers.authors: Kharitonova A, Metcalf R, Lawless W, Patel RS, Wang B, Guida WC, Patel NA.
papers.abstract: Stimulator of Interferon Genes (STING) is a central mediator of innate immune signaling and a therapeutic target for inflammatory diseases. Previously, we identified Clonixeril (CXL) as a concentration-dependent inhibitory modulator of human STING (hSTING) signaling. Despite structural conservation, murine STING (mSTING) and hSTING differ in ligand recognition and activation. We posit that CXL may exhibit distinct activity in the murine system. Mice are used in biomedical research due to their genetic similarities to humans and their utility in evaluating systemic activity and safety of therapeutic compounds. We evaluated CXL effects on mSTING using computational modeling, as well as in vitro and in vivo studies. Molecular dynamics simulations and induced-fit docking predicted favorable CXL binding to mSTING. In 3T3-L1 cells, CXL enhanced DMXAA-induced STING, TBK1, and IRF3 phosphorylation and IFN-β mRNA expression, showing STING pathway activation. Acute CXL efficacy was evaluated in vivo in C57BL/6 mice. CXL increased IFN-β following DMXAA administration. Histopathology showed no treatment-associated abnormalities. HPLC detected CXL in serum and liver. The study identified species-specific responses, suggesting that mouse models may not accurately reflect the effects of CXL on hSTING signaling. Acute CXL treatment was well-tolerated, and CXL is a positive modulator of DMXAA-induced mSTING signaling in vivo.

papers.title: The Immunological Biography of the Carotid Plaque: From Trained Immunity and Clonal Lymphocytes to Spatial Immune Niches and Plaque Vulnerability.
papers.authors: Krasiński Z, Raffa GM, Kowalewski M, Krasińska B, Pisano C, Cannata S, Suwalski P, Urbanowicz T.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic carotid plaques are shaped by years of interaction between systemic risk factors, hematopoietic conditioning, vascular injury, and local immune responses, yet conventional assessment captures only a limited snapshot of this biological history. This review introduces the concept of the "immunological biography" of the carotid plaque and examines how trained innate immunity, macrophage state and defective resolution, adaptive immune memory, T- and B-cell clonal selection, and spatially organized immune niches contribute to plaque heterogeneity and vulnerability. The literature was identified through a structured PubMed search complemented by reference screening, with emphasis on human carotid tissue, paired blood-plaque studies, immune-repertoire analyses, and single-cell and spatial technologies. Current evidence indicates that immune-cell abundance alone incompletely characterizes plaque biology: functional state, antigen experience, clonality, tissue localization, and interactions with vascular and stromal cells provide additional levels of biological information. We propose the Carotid Plaque Immune Phenotype (CPIP) as an integrative framework linking systemic immune history with cellular state, clonal architecture, spatial organization, and clinically relevant plaque features. Combining circulating biomarkers with tissue-resolved immune profiling may ultimately improve biological phenotyping of carotid atherosclerosis and provide a framework for prospective studies linking plaque immune architecture with cerebrovascular events.

papers.title: In Silico Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Senescence-Associated Programs' Progress Along the Normal-Adenoma-Carcinoma Sequence in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang X, Hu W.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) develops through a multistep progression from normal colonic mucosa to adenoma and ultimately carcinoma. However, the cell-type-specific senescence-associated states during this transition remain incompletely understood. We performed an integrative analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomic datasets derived from normal mucosa, adenomatous polyps, and primary CRC tissues. Our analyses revealed a progressive increase in senescence-associated transcriptional scores from normal mucosa through adenoma to carcinoma, with the highest senescence scores observed in malignant tissues. This increase was particularly evident in epithelial cells and monocytes. Cell-cell communication analysis identified enhanced macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) signaling between high-senescence-score cells and B-cell populations, primarily through the MIF-CD74/CXCR4 receptor complex. Spatial transcriptomic analysis further showed that high-senescence-score regions were preferentially localized at or near the tumor invasive margin and in proximity to stromal regions, indicating that senescence-associated programs may contribute to the spatial organization of the CRC microenvironment. Together, these findings support a senescence-centered model of colorectal tumor evolution in which epithelial, myeloid, and lymphoid senescence-associated states progressively accumulate and interact through paracrine signaling networks. The MIF-CD74/CXCR4 axis may represent a candidate mediator of senescence-associated tumor-immune interactions and a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: From Proteostasis Collapse to Endothelial Failure: Mechanistic Pathways Linking Heat Stress, Regulated Cell Death, and Coagulopathy.
papers.authors: Dervišević E, Ajanović T, Čamdžić N, Salerno M, Pomara C, Esposito M, Chisari M, Zorlak A, Selak N, Hodžić E, Sessa F.
papers.abstract: This review proposes an integrative mechanistic model that brings together apoptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, necroptosis, and necrosis within the broader context of heat-induced proteostasis disruption. Rather than depicting a strictly sequential or fully validated causal pathway, the model provides a conceptual framework through which interactions among cellular stress responses, endothelial dysfunction, heatstroke-induced coagulopathy (HIC), and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) may be understood. Under extreme heat stress, widespread protein unfolding and chaperone saturation activate the unfolded protein response, disrupt endoplasmic (ER) calcium homeostasis, and couple through Ca2+-mediated injury to mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. These processes are reciprocally amplifying: reactive oxygen species (ROS) from failing mitochondria deepen proteostatic damage and potentiate necroptotic and ferroptotic signaling, while inflammation-driven immune activation further increases ROS production, closing a self-reinforcing cycle. The resulting engagement of multiple RCD pathways, apoptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and necroptosis, each with qualitatively distinct DAMP signatures, promotes inflammasome activation and a cytokine storm that destabilizes the endothelial glycocalyx, impairs barrier integrity, and triggers a pro-coagulant shift underlying HIC. We further examine biomarker candidates reflecting these mechanisms, evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies, ranging from HSP modulation and antioxidant therapy to endothelial-protective agents, mitophagy regulators, and nanomedicine, and outline the future role of multi-omics, machine learning, and regenerative approaches. By bringing together molecular, cellular, vascular, and systemic processes into a single cohesive model, this review proposes a conceptual foundation to guide diagnostic refinement, therapeutic innovation, and forensic interpretation in severe heat-related injury.

papers.title: Radiation-Induced Remodeling of Bone Metastases and the Bone Marrow Microenvironment: From External-Beam Radiotherapy to Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
papers.authors: Monzen S, Kotani A, Tatara M, Muro A, Fukushi Y, Wojcik A, Mariya Y.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Bone metastases arise within a specialized microenvironment in which tumor cells interact with skeletal, stromal, vascular, immune, and hematopoietic compartments. Radiotherapy therefore affects not only metastatic tumor cells but also the surrounding bone and marrow niches. This review examines radiation-induced remodeling of the bone metastatic and bone marrow microenvironments across external-beam radiotherapy (EBRT) and radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT). Methods: We performed a narrative synthesis of experimental and clinical studies addressing cellular radiosensitivity, skeletal and stromal remodeling, hematopoietic injury, vascular and immune responses, oxidative and metabolic stress, and spatial and temporal patterns of radiation delivery. Emerging transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, lipidomic, single-cell, and spatial approaches were also considered. Results: EBRT and RPT produce overlapping but biologically distinct perturbations because of differences in dose rate, exposure duration, particle range, target localization, microscopic energy deposition, and spatial dose heterogeneity. These differences can influence tumor control, resistance, bone remodeling, and marrow toxicity through effects on osteoblasts, osteoclasts, stromal and vascular cells, immune populations, and HSPCs. These issues are particularly relevant to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers, in which bone seeking and tumor targeting radiopharmaceuticals differentially irradiate cellular compartments within the same skeletal environment. Conclusions: Bone metastases should be viewed as part of a dynamic bone-tumor-marrow microenvironment. Integrating radiation biology, spatial dosimetry, and multi-omics may support more individualized treatment strategies that maximize tumor control while limiting skeletal and hematologic injury.

papers.title: Computer-Aided Drug Design for Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment Reprogramming: A Critical Review.
papers.authors: Moon J, Rew J, Shin HK, Song K, Cho H, Jung J, Kyung M.
papers.abstract: How can cellular interactions in solid tumors guide molecular interventions against immune suppression? This critical review examines how computer-aided drug design (CADD) connects immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) states to testable molecular hypotheses. We distinguish observational artificial intelligence (AI) predictions from molecular intervention hypotheses and examine the experimental evidence required to evaluate them. We reviewed patient-derived models, spatial and multi-omics profiling, molecular design, simulation, and pharmacology using literature identified through 15 October 2026. Adenosine-receptor antagonist discovery and generative protein-binder design illustrated how computational methods contributed to experimentally tested molecular candidates. Native-state structural studies, stromal delivery, and protein degradation broadened the approaches considered. We organized these findings into a proposed framework encompassing in vivo and patient-derived systems, multi-omics mapping, phenotyping of TME states, actionable AI integration, combination-therapy prioritization, and translational testing (IMPACT). A retrospective analysis of a phase III trial illustrated how the framework connects clinical outcomes to questions about mechanism, patient selection, and exposure. The synthesis clarifies the evidence required to connect molecular binding, target engagement, and exposure to patient benefit. IMPACT provides a structure for relating biological context to molecular design and specifying hypotheses for prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Mendelian Randomization Analyses Reveal Novel Genetic Risk Genes of Perivascular Macrophages in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Li Z, Wang M, Li L, Lim KL, Cui W.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive neurovascular dysfunction and neuroinflammation, in which perivascular macrophages (PVMs) serve as key immune sentinels that regulate cerebrovascular homeostasis and disease progression. However, the transcriptional remodeling, genetic susceptibility, and functional mechanisms of PVMs in the pathogenesis of PD remain unclear. In this study, we integrated human midbrain single-nucleus RNA sequencing, genetic association datasets, and transcriptomic analyses to characterize PVM alterations in PD. Through multi-omics analyses, including Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and trajectory inference, we identified PD-associated PVM genes and regulatory pathways, which were further validated in a rotenone-induced PD model. We found extensive transcriptional remodeling of PVMs in PD, manifested by inflammatory activation, altered complement signaling, and aberrant neurovascular interactions. Genetic analyses identified HLA-DRA, OSBPL3, and RIN3 as PD-associated PVM genes that were enriched in PVMs and exhibited dynamic changes during disease progression. Functional analyses suggested that these genes are involved in immune regulation, lipid metabolism, and intracellular trafficking. The rotenone-induced model further confirmed the upregulation of Osbpl3 and Rin3. These findings reveal that PVM-centered neurovascular immune remodeling is a feature of PD and identify HLA-DRA, OSBPL3, and RIN3 as candidate genes supported by genetic evidence, linking PVM dysfunction to PD susceptibility.

papers.title: Cross-Tissue Concordance of a T1D Blood-Derived B-Cell Signature with Hashimoto Thyroiditis Tissue: Exploratory Spatial Immune-Topic Analysis.
papers.authors: Joo EY, Lee SH.
papers.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) and Hashimoto thyroiditis (HT) share autoimmune features, but cross-tissue concordance of B-cell transcriptional programs remains uncertain. Using 24 retained cohort-pathway effect estimates, we recalculated T1D blood summary-level meta-analysis statistics and separately report the previously generated frozen 14-gene HT thyroid association. The T1D meta-analysis yielded Hedges' g = 0.51 (95% CI 0.18-0.85; q = 0.022; I2 = 0%). In HRA001684 (16 HT, 50 non-HT), the frozen score was associated with HT (HC3-adjusted β = 2.65, 95% CI 2.37-2.94; permutation P = 2 × 10-5). Single-cell data (6512 cells; three HT and three immune-checkpoint-inhibitor-associated thyroiditis libraries) lacked healthy controls and were analyzed descriptively. In five spatial sections, the frozen-signature contrast was nonsignificant (Δ = 0.459; exact P = 0.10; matched-gene P = 0.085), with no preferential correspondence to B/plasma-cell topics (reported P = 0.90). Independently inferred thyroid immune topics showed regional variation but did not localize the frozen score. These reported findings are compatible with partial T1D blood-HT thyroid transcriptional concordance but do not establish systemic HT activation, a shared cell-intrinsic program, or validated spatial localization. In the reported sensitivity analysis, joint B-cell/plasma-cell marker adjustment attenuated the HT association by approximately 90%, with the fully adjusted confidence interval including zero. Comparisons with equal weighting and other B-cell reference signatures did not establish a statistically significant advantage of the T1D-derived weights. The public GitHub workflow verifies summary-level pooling of retained effects only; source-to-result reconstruction of the HT bulk, spatial, single-cell, and marker/weight analyses has not been established.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Radiomics Analyses Identify N-Acetylneuraminate Synthase ( NANS )-High Signature Associated with Adverse Prognosis and Immune Remodeling in Glioblastoma.
papers.authors: Chen J, Wu Q, Cardenas HM, Bernard KN, Berglund AE, Sun Y, Macaulay RJ, Mulé JJ, Etame AB.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by marked heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. N-acetylneuraminate synthase (NANS) contributes to tumor-associated metabolic regulation, but its relationship with GBM and its immune profile remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize the prognostic and immune relevance of NANS and develop an MRI radiomics model for noninvasive prediction of NANS-high GBM. Prognostic genes were screened across TCGA-GBM and two CGGA cohorts. Bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses were used to evaluate NANS expression, patient survival association, and cellular localization. NANS-high bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were characterized using functional enrichment and CellChat analyses. A NANS-high BMDM signature was validated in TCGA-GBM for immune infiltration and ligand-receptor axis activity. Drug sensitivity and CMap analyses were performed. MRI radiomics features were extracted from preprocessed T1 contrast-enhanced and FLAIR images, and an elastic net logistic regression model was constructed to predict NANS-high BMDM signature status. NANS was identified as a prognostic macrophage-associated biomarker in GBM and was enriched in BMDMs. NANS-high BMDMs showed enrichment of mTORC1 signaling, oxidative phosphorylation, unfolded protein response, glycolysis, hypoxia, and protein secretion programs. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed enhanced outgoing signaling toward malignant tumor states and T-cell subsets, with LGALS9-centered interactions representing the dominant differential communication program. In TCGA-GBM, the NANS-high BMDM signature correlated with increased macrophage infiltration, broad immune infiltration, and elevated LGALS9 and PLAU axis scores. Drug sensitivity analyses suggested potential vulnerabilities involving PI3K/mTOR and MAPK/ERK pathways. The radiomics model selected six MRI features and distinguished NANS-high from NANS-low tumors with an AUC of 0.795 (95% CI, 0.652-0.939); bootstrap validation showed a mean AUC of 0.793 (95% CI, 0.637-0.922). NANS-high BMDMs define a prognostically adverse and potentially targetable macrophage-associated phenotype in GBM. MRI radiomics may noninvasively predict this NANS-high BMDM state, supporting imaging-based risk stratification and therapeutic selection.

papers.title: Activation of Innate and Adaptive Immunity in the Central Nervous System Following Xenogeneic Mesenchymal Stromal Cell Transplantation.
papers.authors: Norte-Muñoz M, Cantón-Sandoval J, Lucas-Ruiz F, Mulero V, Agudo-Barriuso M, García-Bernal D.
papers.abstract: Stem cell-based therapies have emerged as promising strategies for neurodegenerative disorders, partly supported by the concept of central nervous system immune privilege, which has encouraged xenogeneic transplantation approaches under the assumption of limited host immune responses. However, the immunological consequences of xenogeneic cell delivery into the central nervous system remain poorly characterized. In this study, we investigated the immune response elicited by intravitreal transplantation of human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (BM-MSCs) into healthy mouse retinas. Twenty-one days after transplantation, retinal CD45+ and/or CD11b+ cells, including microglia, macrophages, and infiltrating leukocytes, were isolated and subjected to exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing. Candidate immune cell populations and pathways identified transcriptomically were subsequently evaluated by immunostaining, flow cytometry, and plasma antibody analyses. Xenogeneic BM-MSC transplantation induced marked transcriptional changes consistent with immune activation, enhanced antigen presentation, and leukocyte recruitment, features that are not typically associated with central nervous system homeostasis. These findings were supported by complementary cellular and systemic analyses, collectively revealing innate and adaptive immune responses directed against the transplanted human cells. The results demonstrate that xenogeneic BM-MSC transplantation can overcome local immune regulatory mechanisms and trigger robust immune activation within the healthy retina. These findings identify previously underappreciated immunological barriers to xenogeneic stem cell-based therapies and reveal coordinated innate and adaptive immune responses despite the presumed immune privilege of the CNS. Consideration of these immune responses will be essential for the safe and effective translation of regenerative therapies.

papers.title: Construction of a GCSCs-Related Prognostic Risk Model Based on Transcriptomic Data.
papers.authors: Hu X, Fan S, Liu N, Fan M, Wu Y, Shi G, Su Y, Liu L, Chen X.
papers.abstract: Gastric Cancer Stem Cells (GCSCs) contribute to tumor progression and treatment resistance, but their heterogeneity and tumor microenvironment interactions remain unclear. We analyzed GSE163558 single-cell RNA-sequencing data from 10 gastric cancer samples and integrated GCSC-related genes with The Cancer Genome Atlas Stomach Adenocarcinoma (TCGA-STAD) training cohort (n = 448) and two independent external validation cohorts, GSE62254 (n = 300) and GSE84437 (n = 483), to construct and validate a six-gene prognostic risk model. Cell-cell communication, metabolic activity, immune infiltration, immunotherapy response, and drug sensitivity were evaluated. Nine cell populations, including a putative GCSC population, were identified. GCSCs showed higher inferred oxidative phosphorylation activity and extensive predicted interactions with tumor-associated cells. The model stratified patients into distinct prognostic groups. High-risk tumors exhibited enrichment of progression-related pathways, including epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and distinct immune features. In PRJEB25780 (n = 78), higher risk scores were associated with immunotherapy non-response, whereas an exploratory analysis of GSE91061 (n = 49) showed a similar trend. The model may support prognostic stratification and provide insights into potential associations with therapeutic response, pending prospective validation.

papers.title: Matrix-Associated Gene Expression and Annotated Tumor-Stroma Composition of Transcriptomically Defined Cold Regions in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Lituma-Gonzalez WD, Arunprasad AV, Chancay H, Jayavelan V, Chakravadhanula M, Ballaz S, Lakshmanan S.
papers.abstract: Regional transcriptomic labels can reflect cell mixtures and expression states. We examined how transcriptomically defined cold regions in triple-negative breast cancer relate to matrix-associated expression, annotated composition, spatial neighborhoods, and cell-type attribution. We reanalyzed public data from 43 discovery sections (22 patients) and 11 cancer captures of a secondary dataset with discovery-derived labels. Computational spot labels included desert (D), excluded (E), inflamed (I), and ambiguous-cold. Hierarchical models estimated E-D contrasts and E-I gene contrasts with and without sequencing-depth and estimated tumor-abundance adjustment; tests underwent Holm correction. Further analyses addressed annotated composition, neighborhoods, and pooled exploratory cell-type attribution. Estimated cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) abundance was higher in E- than D-labeled regions (standardized within-section effect 0.78; 95% confidence interval 0.55-1.00), as was expression of PDGFRB, COL3A1, COL5A1, and COL6A1; the three collagen genes remained higher than in D- and I-labeled regions after adjustment. Across 11 captures, the median within-capture difference in tumor-annotated spot fraction (E minus D) was -14.1 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval -33.5 to -10.7; nine negative, two ties; interval reached zero without in situ annotations). In discovery, 330 of 822 ambiguous cold spots neighbored both D- and E-labeled spots, exceeding two null models. Pooled models estimated positive COL3A1 and COL5A1 differences within CAFs; immune readouts depended on scoring and adjustment. We characterized a stromal-transcriptomic contrast: E-labeled regions showed higher matrix-associated expression and estimated CAF abundance than D-labeled regions and, in the secondary dataset, lower annotated tumor fraction. These measurements refine interpretation without implying functional immune exclusion.

papers.title: The Impact of Intratumoral Bacterial Response to Vaccine Therapy in Cancer Treatment.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Sun ZJ, Qi HL, Zhao D, Xing XD, Jiang JD, Gao TL.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic Human papillomavirus (HPVs) vaccines are designed to enhance the immunogenicity of HPV and promote the elimination of tumor cells effectively. Mounting evidence implies that tumor-resident microbiomes may influence therapeutic outcomes through immune modulation. In this study, we evaluated whether the intratumoral microbiota affects the efficacy of the therapeutic HPV vaccine. We analyzed RNA sequencing data from tumor tissues of C57BL/6N female mice treated with a DNA vaccine incorporating HPV16 E6/E7 antigens fused with the chemokine CCL11. Microbial community data were acquired using the PathSeq bioinformatics pipeline. Alpha diversity was estimated using the Shannon index and the number of observed taxonomic features, while beta diversity was assessed via principal coordinate analysis (PCoA) based on Bray-Curtis distance. Linear discriminant analysis Effect Size (LEfSe) analysis was performed to identify differentially abundant microbial taxa. Immune cell infiltration was characterized using the xCell deconvolution method. The analysis revealed significant divergence in both the alpha- and beta-diversity metrics of intratumoral microbiota, associated with treatment responsiveness. Vaccinated groups exhibited enriched abundances of the phyla Proteobacteria, together with a concomitant reduction in Firmicutes and Actinobacteria, and were associated with a positive response to cancer immunotherapy. Additionally, intratumoral microbiome composition and diversity correlated with the increased infiltration of CD8+ T cells, natural killer T (NKT) cells, and myeloid cells. This study identifies intratumoral microbiota remodeling as a key feature of therapeutic HPV vaccine response. The observed coordination between bacterial signatures and immune cell infiltration is associative and raises the hypothesis that intratumoral bacteria may modulate, rather than drive, antitumor immunity. These findings support the development of intratumoral microbiota profiling and highlight the potential for microbiota-targeted strategies to enhance cancer immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Ferroptosis-Related Gene Signature Underlying Macrophage Heterogeneity and Immune Dysregulation in Rheumatoid Arthritis Synovium.
papers.authors: Liu H, Zhang R.
papers.abstract: Ferroptosis contributes to rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the key regulators and their cell-specific functions in the synovial microenvironment remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify robust ferroptosis-associated biomarkers and define their cellular context through an integrated transcriptomic framework. Bulk synovial transcriptomic datasets were integrated using differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and a curated ferroptosis gene set. Candidate genes were prioritized using three feature-selection algorithms and validated across twelve models. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, pseudotime, CellChat, and virtual gene perturbation analyses characterized their cellular and functional context. Six ferroptosis-related genes (AIM2, HCP5, CAPG, ALOX5, TYMS, and RUNX3) formed a diagnostic signature discriminating RA from healthy synovium (mean leakage-free test AUC 0.977 across five training-only re-derivations; 0.9375 in the primary split), with consistent leave-one-dataset-out and osteoarthritis-control validation. These genes linked to adaptive immune and ferroptosis-associated transcriptional programs. Single-cell analysis localized this transcriptional score to macrophages, where ferroptosis-signature-high macrophages occupied a central communication-network position and showed collagen-pathway enrichment; because RA and healthy samples were not fully independent of dataset origin, this finding is hypothesis-generating. Pseudotime analysis suggested progressive induction of these genes toward an inflammatory NF-κB/TNF/IL-17 terminal state, and virtual perturbation suggested convergence on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation networks that persisted after removing sex-chromosome genes, though residual sex-associated effects cannot be fully excluded. This study identifies a biologically interpretable ferroptosis-related gene signature and suggests ferroptosis-associated macrophage reprogramming may contribute to immune dysregulation in RA synovium. The single-cell findings are hypothesis-generating given the cohort design, while the diagnostic signature was supported by leakage-free, cross-cohort, and disease-specificity analyses, providing candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets for RA.

papers.title: Integrated Bulk Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Reveal Extracellular-Matrix Remodeling and Tubular Metabolic Failure in ADPKD Progression.
papers.authors: Chen C, Lei L, Xu Y, Chen Z.
