papers.abstract: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) progression involves cyst expansion, interstitial remodeling, and progressive loss of renal function, but the cell-type-resolved programs linking cyst burden to tissue remodeling remain incompletely defined. We integrated the cyst-size-stratified human bulk transcriptomic dataset GSE7869 with the time-resolved Pkd1 single-cell dataset GSE268494. Differentially expressed genes were identified across small-, middle- and large-cyst groups, modeled by Mfuzz temporal clustering, prioritized by protein-protein interaction topology and functional enrichment, and further evaluated by immune deconvolution, single-cell mapping, AUCell pathway scoring and CellPhoneDB ligand-receptor inference. We identified 3842 shared differentially expressed genes and two dominant monotonic modules. The progressively upregulated module was enriched for extracellular-matrix organization, adhesion, and fibrosis-associated genes, including COL1A1, COL5A2, FBN1, BGN, LAMC1, HSPG2, MMP2, LOX, and ITGA5. The progressively downregulated module highlighted tubular transport, proton transport, and mitochondrial/metabolic genes, including SLC12A3, AQP2, ATP5A1, ATP6V0C, ATP6V1B1, NDUFV1, REN, and AGT. Single-cell analyses localized the matrix module mainly to fibroblast/stromal compartments and the transport/metabolic module to segment-specific tubular epithelial populations. Immune deconvolution and ligand-receptor inference further implicated macrophage-associated remodeling and TGFB1-, CD47-, CD200-, PECAM1- and TNF-superfamily-related immune-parenchymal communication. ADPKD progression is associated with coordinated ECM/immune remodeling and tubular metabolic failure, providing candidate markers and communication axes for future spatial and functional validation.

papers.title: Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) and Fungal Antigen Presentation: Immunological Mechanisms and Their Role in Anti-Fungal Immunity.
papers.authors: Shu F, Khamto N, Amsri A, Youngchim S, Nosanchuk JD, Chum-In T, Deng Q, Pruksaphon K.
papers.abstract: Cellular-mediated immunity against invasive fungal infections is fundamentally governed by Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) restriction, whereby T cells detect fungal invasion indirectly through peptide fragments displayed on host MHC molecules rather than by recognizing intact fungal pathogens. In contrast to B cells, which bind native microbial antigens, T lymphocytes monitor antigen-presenting cells for processed fungal peptides presented by MHC class I and class II molecules. This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying fungal antigen processing and presentation, emphasizing the pivotal contributions of MHC class II-restricted CD4 T-helper (TH1/TH17) cells and cross-presented, MHC class I-restricted CD8 cytotoxic T lymphocytes to antifungal host defense. We also summarize key experimental approaches, including overlapping peptide libraries, ELISpot assays, and peptide-MHC multimers, for defining MHC function and identifying immunodominant fungal antigenic determinants. Evidence from representative pathogenic fungal antigens, including Asp f16, Crf1, Eng2, and the multivalent rCpa1 vaccine, highlights both the promise and complexity of achieving cross-protective cellular immunity. Importantly, amino acid sequence similarity alone is insufficient to predict T-cell cross-reactivity, indicating that computational prediction and experimental epitope mapping should be employed as complementary approaches for the accurate identification and validation of immunologically relevant epitopes. Finally, elucidating the molecular principles governing fungal peptide presentation establishes a rational foundation for the development of broadly protective epitope-based vaccines and next-generation immunotherapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics in Chronic Rhinosinusitis: Deciphering Tissue Architecture, Immune Niches, and Precision Therapeutics.
papers.authors: Ghosh S, Madar IH, Bardhan K, Muruganantham P.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disorder in which epithelial injury, immune activation, and stromal remodelling are organised into local tissue niches. Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing have defined important cell states, but dissociation removes the anatomical relationships needed to determine where those states coexist. Spatial transcriptomics (ST) addresses this gap by mapping RNA, and in some platforms, protein, onto intact sinonasal tissue. This review provides an evidence-graded synthesis organised around a single translational chain: spatial niche to molecular signature to plausible biological mechanism to CRS phenotype/endotype to clinical implication to therapeutic relevance to validation status. Direct CRS ST evidence is separated from single-cell RNA sequencing support, computational prediction, protein or in situ evidence, experimental perturbation, clinical validation, and extrapolation from other inflammatory diseases. Current CRS studies support spatial compartmentalisation of eosinophil-rich epithelial lesions, ALOX15-positive macrophage programmes, GZMK-positive CD8 T-cell-fibroblast neighbourhoods, and treatment-associated epithelial and stromal changes. However, most ligand-receptor calls remain predictive, and spatial association alone does not establish functional causality. ST is therefore best viewed as a discovery and mechanistic-prioritisation technology whose clinical promises-biomarker selection, biologic matching, and response monitoring-require independent cohorts, locked assays, patient-level reproducibility, and prospective outcome studies. We compare study designs and platforms, examine statistical issues including spatial autocorrelation and pseudoreplication, and propose a cautious translational framework in which orthogonal and clinical validation convert spatial observations into actionable evidence.

papers.title: A Lymphoid-Enriched Spatial Immune Niche Defines an Immunotherapy-Responsive State in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Cai M, Hu K, Wang H, Li J, Wu Y, Han Q, Chen J, Zhong W, Huang X, Ding F, Du Y, Liu Y, Zhang F.
papers.abstract: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a first-line therapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet only a subset of patients achieve durable benefit. The spatial organization of the tumour microenvironment (TME) and its relationship to immunotherapy response remain incompletely understood. We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, and bulk RNA-sequencing cohorts to characterize spatially organized immune ecosystems associated with immunotherapy response in HCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing from 100 HCC samples was used to construct a cellular reference, which was integrated with spatial transcriptomics from 12 sections to identify nine consensus spatial niches. Niche 9 represented a lymphoid-enriched immune state characterized by B cells, plasma cells, natural killer cells, T-cell subsets, macrophages, and tertiary lymphoid structure-associated transcriptional features. Independent validation in a pretreatment, response-annotated Visium cohort showed enrichment of Niche 9-associated transcriptional activity in immunotherapy responders, while spatially co-registered 51-plex CODEX profiling provided orthogonal protein-level support for its lymphoid and immune-enriched phenotype. Multi-omics characterization further revealed coordinated immune-cell localization, ligand-receptor-associated patterns, and distinct metabolic programmes, with MEI1-positive plasma cells displaying enhanced secretory and stress-adaptation states. A nine-gene transcriptional signature derived from Niche 9 was associated with atezolizumab-plus-bevacizumab response, enhanced lymphoid immune features, lower Tumour Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion scores, and favourable clinical outcomes in independent cohorts. These multi-cohort and multi-omics analyses define a spatially derived lymphoid-enriched immune programme and link its molecular features to immunotherapy sensitivity in HCC.

papers.title: Structural and Biophysical Profiling of HLA Class II Mismatches Using AlphaFold 3: A Computational Study.
papers.authors: Bardash V, Samchuk O, Tolstyak Y, Demydenko H, Sklyarov E.
papers.abstract: Conventional linear eplet-matching algorithms (HLAMatchmaker, HLAMM) evaluate primary sequence polymorphisms across human leukocyte antigen (HLA) loci without integrating three-dimensional (3D) steric accessibility and local physicochemical constraints. Here, we developed an exploratory computational antigenicity pipeline using AlphaFold 3 to evaluate 10,000 simulated European donor-recipient pairs across pre-computed, full-length HLA class I (HLA-A, -B, -C) and heterodimeric class II (HLA-DR, -DQ, -DP) complexes modeled in a standardized peptide-free conformation. Candidate eplets were sequentially screened using a spatial solvent-accessible surface area threshold (SASA ≥ 10.0 Å2) and an empirical biophysical exclusion gate (5th percentile of absolute net charge |Qnet| ≥ 0.3326 e and hydropathy Htotal ≥ -7.265, calibrated on N = 170 antibody-verified eplets). Across the simulated cohort (n = 10,000), filtration reduced median [Q1; Q3] eplet counts from 19 [12; 26] to 17 [10; 23] for HLA-A, 22 [15; 29] to 18 [12; 24] for HLA-B, 12 [7; 17] to 10 [7; 15] for HLA-C, 15 [10; 19] to 11 [7; 14] for HLA-DR, 12 [6; 17] to 9 [4; 14] for HLA-DQ, and 7 [3; 12] to 6 [2; 9] for HLA-DP. Component ablation demonstrated that 3D steric accessibility (SASA ≥ 10.0 Å2) accounted for the vast majority of eplet exclusions-87.8% in HLA-DR and HLA-DP and 58.2% to 69.1% across HLA-DQ and class I loci-whereas the registry-calibrated biophysical gate acted as a secondary refinement. Within the subset of simulated pairs initially exceeding the arbitrary ≥10-eplet linear cutoff, the proportion dropping below 10 eplets after filtering was low for class I (HLA-A: 4.4%, HLA-B: 8.0%, HLA-C: 13.2%) but substantially higher for class II high-load subsets: HLA-DQ (21.8%), HLA-DR (26.0%), and HLA-DP (33.7% of 3693 baseline high-load pairs). Furthermore, class II loci, particularly HLA-DP, exhibited weakened covariance between heuristic charge and hydropathy indices that persisted after 1:1 count-matched subsampling (ρmatched = -0.268) and partial correlation adjustment (ρpartial = -0.385). This dual-filter pipeline defines a restricted mathematical subset of spatially accessible and biophysically suprathreshold candidate eplets. Because this is a hypothesis-generating in silico framework, multicenter retrospective registry analyses and prospective clinical trials evaluating de novo donor-specific antibody formation, biopsy-proven rejection, and allograft survival are strictly required before clinical translation.

papers.title: Vascular and Immune Cell Interactions in Atherosclerosis: Mechanisms, Plaque Destabilization, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.authors: Zhou Y, Xiao K, Chen Y, He Y, Liu Y, Zhang W, Zhang Y, Dong Z, Guo Z, Li J, Wei J.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a progressive vascular disease characterized by lipid accumulation within the arterial intima, chronic inflammation, and plaque formation. It represents the underlying pathological basis of major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, including coronary artery disease, acute myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke. Accumulating evidence suggests that the initiation and progression of AS are not driven by dysfunction of a single cell type but rather result from complex and dynamic interactions among multiple vascular resident and immune cells, including endothelial cells (ECs), vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), macrophages, and lymphocytes. This review systematically summarizes the functional and phenotypic characteristics of these four major cell types in atherosclerotic lesions, with particular emphasis on their bidirectional regulatory networks. We provide an in-depth analysis of key intercellular communication mechanisms, including paracrine signaling, exosome-mediated transfer, oxidative stress crosstalk, and autophagy regulation, all of which play central roles in plaque microenvironment remodeling, lipid core expansion, fibrous cap degradation, and plaque destabilization. Furthermore, we highlight recent advances in translational strategies targeting cell-cell interactions, focusing on the mechanisms of action and clinical potential of representative agents.

papers.title: Immune and Circulating Biomarkers in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Prognostic and Predictive Relevance for Immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Sidhom F, Karabiber E, ElBeblawy R, Babagiray A, Yacoub T, El-Rayes B, Akce M.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based combinations have become the standard first-line systemic therapy, yet objective response rates remain modest (20-36%), and no HCC-specific immune biomarker has been validated to guide selection among standard ICI-based regimens. This review examines the prognostic and exploratory treatment-response associations of potential immune biomarkers in HCC, including markers within the tumor microenvironment (TME) and peripheral blood. A narrative review was conducted evaluating PD-L1 and soluble PD-L1, tumor mutational burden (TMB), tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), including machine learning-based assessment, gene expression profiles and tumor-intrinsic pathway alterations, long non-coding RNAs, inflammatory markers (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, alpha-fetoprotein), gut microbiota, and liquid biopsy analytes (circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, cell-free DNA). PD-L1 expression shows prognostic associations and inconsistent associations with ICI outcomes; inter-assay heterogeneity further limits its use, and routine PD-L1 testing is not recommended by current guidelines. TMB is generally low in HCC, with inconsistent associations with ICI response. High CD8+ TIL density is associated with improved survival after resection and favorable outcomes in exploratory ICI-treated cohorts, without validated treatment-selective utility. Inflammatory gene signatures and WNT/β-catenin pathway activation are associated with ICI outcomes. Gut microbiome features have shown exploratory associations with anti-PD-1 outcomes, with limited consistency across small datasets. Liquid biopsy markers, particularly ctDNA, show promise for recurrence prediction and treatment monitoring but lack assay standardization. Multiple immune biomarkers demonstrate prognostic value in HCC, and pre-existing immunity characterized by high CD8+ T-cell infiltration and inflammatory gene signatures is associated with improved ICI-based therapy outcomes in exploratory studies. However, these exploratory markers have not been validated for routine selection among HCC regimens. Future directions include prospective validation of composite biomarker panels, standardization of assessment methodologies, and integration of artificial intelligence for TME characterization.

papers.title: The Broadly Neutralizing DEV_K57 Antibody, Isolated from a Convalescent Patient, in Complex with the SARS-CoV-2 RBD.
papers.authors: Sinitsina EV, Imatdinov IR, Tuyrin VY, Shipovalov AV, Zaykovskaya AV, Osinkina IA, Yanshin AO, Radchenko NS, Ryzhykau YL, Sudarev VV, Kuklina DD, Onkhonova GS, Ivleva EK, Agafonov AP, Gladysheva AV.
papers.abstract: The continuous evolution of SARS-CoV-2 necessitates broadly neutralizing antibodies for robust therapeutics. In this study, we isolated 1824 single B cells from a COVID-19 convalescent donor and obtained 91 pairs of nucleotide sequences potentially encoding VH/VL domains. From this library, we generated and evaluated a panel of 38 recombinant monoclonal antibodies. Among this panel, we identified DEV_K57 as a broadly neutralizing human IgG1 antibody targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. DEV_K57 exhibited in vitro neutralization breadth against diverse variants, demonstrating subnanomolar IC50 values. This in vitro efficacy was translated in vivo. In a Syrian hamster model of SARS-CoV-2 Delta infection, DEV_K57 significantly reduced viral RNA and infectious titers in both the upper and lower respiratory tracts, conferring a favorable safety profile with minimal histopathological damage. To elucidate its mechanism, we performed comprehensive biophysical and structural analyses. Biolayer interferometry revealed a high picomolar binding affinity to the RBD Delta. Furthermore, size-exclusion chromatography coupled with small-angle X-ray scattering and computational modeling uncovered a unique, stable dimeric architecture of the DEV_K57 Fab-RBD complex in solution, with a binding interface distinct from previously characterized structures. These findings underscore the value of rapid antibody isolation for pandemic preparedness against future emerging biological threats.

papers.title: Immune Remodeling Across Advanced Heart Failure, LVAD Support, and Heart Transplantation: From Cellular Activation to Tissue-Resident Memory.
papers.authors: Krasiński Z, Urbanowicz T, Kowalewski M, Raffa GM, Krasińska B, Pisano C, Manca P, Rahnama M, Suwalski P, Gosik K, Grywalska E.
papers.abstract: Advanced heart failure (HF) left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support and heart transplantation (HTx) are commonly considered distinct clinical stages, although each occurs within an immune system shaped by preceding inflammatory and antigenic exposures. This review introduces the concept of the recipient immune biography, describing the cumulative immunological history that accompanies patients from advanced HF through mechanical circulatory support to transplantation. We examine how HF-associated innate and adaptive immune activation may be modified by mechanical unloading while simultaneously being reshaped by blood-device interactions, hemolysis, complement activation, infection, transfusion, and sensitization during LVAD support. Following transplantation, this preconditioned immune repertoire encounters persistent donor alloantigen through direct, indirect, and semidirect allorecognition. We integrate T-cell effector, regulatory, exhaustion-associated, and memory states with T follicular helper-B-cell interactions, plasma-cell persistence, donor-specific antibodies, and tissue-resident immunity. Emphasis is placed on the limitations of peripheral biomarkers for representing graft-localized immune processes. We propose a Longitudinal Immune Trajectory integrating serial peripheral biomarkers with cellular, clonal, molecular, and spatial profiling to reconstruct patient-specific immune remodeling across the HF-LVAD-HTx continuum.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Screening and Experimental Validation of PIK3C2A as a Candidate Angiogenesis-Related Molecule in Pulmonary Hypertension.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Zhao D, Xiao H, Gao L, Huang L, Bai D, Gou D, Zhang S.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling and dysregulated angiogenesis. However, the angiogenesis-related molecular mechanisms underlying PH remain incompletely understood, and reliable diagnostic biomarkers are still lacking. Therefore, To identify angiogenesis-related key molecules in PH through integrated transcriptomic analyses and experimental validation, we aimed to establish a candidate molecular signature and evaluate the discriminative potential of PIK3C2A. Specifically, GSE15197 was used as the primary bulk-transcriptomic discovery dataset, whereas GSE1909 for cross-species validation, and human pulmonary artery single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE210248) for cellular characterization. Moreover, Functional enrichment, Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), immune infiltration analysis, and three machine learning algorithms-logistic regression, random forest (RF), and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) were performed to identify model genes. In addition, Single-cell analyses were performed using GSE210248, followed by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) validation of candidate-gene expression in monocrotaline (MCT) and Sugen5416 plus hypoxia (SuHx) rat models. As a result, Forty-three angiogenesis-related differentially expressed genes (ARDEGs) were identified and were enriched in terms and pathways related to angiogenesis, vascular development, extracellular matrix organization, and HIF-1 signaling. Four model genes (DCN, DKK1, PIK3C2A, and UNC5B) were identified and showed moderate-to-high discrimination between PH and control samples in GSE15197. Among these genes, PIK3C2A showed its highest expression in endothelial cells, while complementary immune-infiltration and CellChat (version 2.1.1) analyses characterized the broader immune-stromal context of the angiogenesis-related signature. qRT-PCR further confirmed significant downregulation of PIK3C2A in the lungs and pulmonary arteries of MCTand SuHxinduced PH models (p < 0.05). In conclusion, An angiogenesis-related candidate molecular signature comprising DCN, DKK1, PIK3C2A and UNC5B was identified in PH. Among these genes, PIK3C2A showed preferential endothelial expression and was downregulated in both the MCT and SuHx rat PH models, supporting its further evaluation as a candidate molecule associated with PH.

papers.title: Maternal obesity primes fetal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells toward myeloid differentiation in a nonhuman primate model.
papers.authors: Doratt BM, Hemati H, Wagner SB, Blanton MB, Avila U, Varlamov O, Messaoudi I.
papers.abstract: Maternal obesity is a major global health challenge with profound consequences for offspring health. While its impact on metabolic programming has been widely studied, far less is known about how maternal factors influence fetal hematopoiesis and immune ontogeny. In this study, we examined fetal bone marrow (FBM) hematopoiesis in a nonhuman primate model of spontaneous maternal obesity maintained on a standard chow diet. In the present study, 6 lean (2 female, 4 male offspring) and 7 spontaneously obese (4 female, 3 male offspring) 8- to 12-year-old female rhesus macaques fed regular chow underwent time-mated breeding. FBM cells were assessed using spectral flow cytometry, single-cell transcriptional profiling, response to stimulation, in vitro differentiation and mitochondrial membrane potential. Spectral flow cytometry demonstrated that maternal obesity altered abundance and composition of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), committed progenitors, and mature immune cell populations. Single-cell transcriptional profiling followed by pseudotime analysis revealed enrichment of early progenitor states with reduced representation of later differentiation states, accompanied by inflammatory transcriptional reprogramming characterized by increased expression of alarmins and interferon‑stimulated genes, particularly within myeloid progenitors. Cell-cell communication analyses predicted altered inflammatory signaling within hematopoietic niche. Functionally, HSPCs from the obese group exhibited enhanced priming for myeloid differentiation under in vitro differentiation conditions. Myeloid progenitors also displayed increased mitochondrial membrane potential, consistent with transcriptional metabolic reprogramming, whereas in vitro-differentiated monocytes exhibited altered lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induced cytokine response, characterized by reduced production of multiple analytes but increased tumor necrosis factor (TNF) production. Together, these results indicate that maternal obesity, even in absence of an obesogenic diet, is associated with remodeling of fetal hematopoietic development by altering HSPC composition, enriching immature differentiation-competent progenitor states, enhancing myeloid differentiation potential under myeloid-promoting conditions, and inducing transcriptional and functional changes in inflammatory responses. These findings provide new insight into how maternal obesity programs fetal hematopoiesis and may contribute to long-term alterations in offspring immune function.
